claim: Somatic cells age and die, but the germ-cell lineage is immortal.
source: Somatic cells age and die, but the germ-cell lineage is immortal.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge about the distinction between somatic and germ cells.

claim: In Caenorhabditis elegans, germline immortality involves proteostasis renewal at the beginning of each new generation.
source: In Caenorhabditis elegans, germline immortality involves proteostasis renewal at the beginning of each new generation, when oocyte maturation signals from sperm trigger the clearance of carbonylated proteins and protein aggregates.
evidence: This claim is supported by the research findings presented in the manuscript and references to prior work.

claim: Oocyte maturation signals from sperm trigger the clearance of carbonylated proteins and protein aggregates.
source: In Caenorhabditis elegans, germline immortality involves proteostasis renewal at the beginning of each new generation, when oocyte maturation signals from sperm trigger the clearance of carbonylated proteins and protein aggregates.
evidence: This is a key finding from prior work that is being built upon in this study.

claim: Oocyte maturation signals are known to trigger protein-aggregate removal via lysosome acidification.
source: Oocyte maturation signals are known to trigger protein-aggregate removal via lysosome acidification.
evidence: This statement references established findings from previous research.

claim: Lysosomes are acidified as a consequence of changes in endoplasmic reticulum activity that permit assembly of the lysosomal V-ATPase.
source: Our findings suggest that lysosomes are acidified as a consequence of changes in endoplasmic reticulum activity that permit assembly of the lysosomal V-ATPase, which in turn allows lysosomes to clear the aggregates via microautophagy.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The lysosomal V-ATPase allows lysosomes to clear aggregates via microautophagy.
source: Our findings suggest that lysosomes are acidified as a consequence of changes in endoplasmic reticulum activity that permit assembly of the lysosomal V-ATPase, which in turn allows lysosomes to clear the aggregates via microautophagy.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental observations.

claim: Mitochondria have two functions in protein aggregation, both of which appear to be independent of ATP generation.
source: We define two functions for mitochondria, both of which appear to be independent of ATP generation.
evidence: This is a key finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Many genes from the screen also regulate lysosome acidification and age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma.
source: Many genes from the screen also regulate lysosome acidification and age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma, suggesting a fundamental mechanistic link between proteostasis renewal in the germline and somatic longevity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: There is a fundamental mechanistic link between proteostasis renewal in the germline and somatic longevity.
source: Many genes from the screen also regulate lysosome acidification and age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma, suggesting a fundamental mechanistic link between proteostasis renewal in the germline and somatic longevity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: An entire oocyte can be eliminated via apoptosis following DNA damage.
source: At one level, an entire oocyte can be eliminated via apoptosis; for example, following DNA damage (Hunter, 2017; Luo et al., 2010; Qiao et al., 2018; Schumacher et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In mice, mitochondria containing defective DNA are eliminated during oogenesis.
source: For example, in mice, mitochondria containing defective DNA are eliminated during oogenesis (Fan et al., 2008), and in yeast, nuclear senescence factors and protein aggregates are extruded during meiosis (King et al., 2019; Unal et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In yeast, nuclear senescence factors and protein aggregates are extruded during meiosis.
source: For example, in mice, mitochondria containing defective DNA are eliminated during oogenesis (Fan et al., 2008), and in yeast, nuclear senescence factors and protein aggregates are extruded during meiosis (King et al., 2019; Unal et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The eggs of Drosophila exhibit enhanced proteasome activity and resistance to protein aggregation relative to the soma.
source: Mechanisms likely exist to counteract protein aggregation in Drosophila as well: relative to the soma, the eggs of Drosophila exhibit enhanced proteasome activity and resistance to protein aggregation (Fredriksson et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Autophagy is required for the survival of the mouse germ lineage.
source: Autophagy, a process known to eliminate damaged organelles and macromolecules, may play a role as well as it is required for the survival of the mouse germ lineage (Gawriluk et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: C. elegans is hermaphroditic, producing both sperm and oocytes in each of two symmetrical gonadal arms.
source: C. elegans is hermaphroditic, producing both sperm and oocytes in each of two symmetrical gonadal arms.
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans biology.

claim: Germ cells originate in stem-cell niches located at the distal ends of each arm and pass through successive stages of meiosis as they move proximally towards the spermatheca, where fertilization occurs.
source: Germ cells originate in stem-cell niches located at the distal ends of each arm and pass through successive stages of meiosis as they move proximally towards the spermatheca, where fertilization occurs (Crittenden et al., 1994; Hubbard and Greenstein, 2005; McCarter et al., 1999; Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Carbonylated proteins are present throughout the distal germline but are eliminated in proximal oocytes.
source: In 2010, Goudeau and Aguilaniu discovered that carbonylated proteins, known to accumulate during aging, are present throughout the distal germline, but are eliminated in proximal oocytes (Goudeau and Aguilaniu, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Mutant worms that lack sperm and develop as females retain carbonylated proteins throughout the entire germline.
source: Mutant worms that lack sperm and develop as females retain carbonylated proteins throughout the entire germline, indicating that sperm play a role in their elimination.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Sperm play a role in the elimination of carbonylated proteins.
source: Mutant worms that lack sperm and develop as females retain carbonylated proteins throughout the entire germline, indicating that sperm play a role in their elimination.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that females lacking sperm retain carbonylated proteins.

claim: Protein aggregates accumulate in the proximal oocytes of females but not in those of hermaphrodites.
source: In addition to carbonylated proteins, protein aggregates also accumulate in the proximal oocytes of females but not in those of hermaphrodites (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Signals from sperm trigger the elimination of protein aggregates in a process that is coupled to the broader choreography of oocyte maturation.
source: Signals from sperm trigger the elimination of protein aggregates in a process that is coupled to the broader choreography of oocyte maturation, which involves dramatic changes in organelle morphology and function (Bluemink et al., 1983; Carroll, 1996; Charbonneau and Grey, 1984; FitzHarris et al., 2007; Kobayashi et al., 1991; Maller et al., 1977; Mehlmann et al., 1995; Wasserman et al., 1982; Yamashita, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Oocyte maturation involves dramatic changes in organelle morphology and function.
source: Signals from sperm trigger the elimination of protein aggregates in a process that is coupled to the broader choreography of oocyte maturation, which involves dramatic changes in organelle morphology and function (Bluemink et al., 1983; Carroll, 1996; Charbonneau and Grey, 1984; FitzHarris et al., 2007; Kobayashi et al., 1991; Maller et al., 1977; Mehlmann et al., 1995; Wasserman et al., 1982; Yamashita, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In C. elegans, oocyte maturation is triggered by actin-like major sperm proteins (MSPs) released from sperm.
source: In C. elegans, oocyte maturation is triggered by actin-like major sperm proteins (MSPs) released from sperm (Kosinski et al., 2005; Miller et al., 2003; Miller et al., 2001) and involves changes in chromosome and nuclear dynamics linked to progression through meiosis, upregulation of translation, and changes in endoplasmic reticulum (ER), lysosomal and mitochondrial function (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017; Huelgas-Morales and Greenstein, 2018; Langerak et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Oocyte maturation involves changes in chromosome and nuclear dynamics linked to progression through meiosis, upregulation of translation, and changes in endoplasmic reticulum (ER), lysosomal and mitochondrial function.
source: In C. elegans, oocyte maturation is triggered by actin-like major sperm proteins (MSPs) released from sperm (Kosinski et al., 2005; Miller et al., 2003; Miller et al., 2001) and involves changes in chromosome and nuclear dynamics linked to progression through meiosis, upregulation of translation, and changes in endoplasmic reticulum (ER), lysosomal and mitochondrial function (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017; Huelgas-Morales and Greenstein, 2018; Langerak et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The shift in lysosomal physiology that occurs during oocyte maturation is crucial for aggregate removal.
source: The shift in lysosomal physiology that occurs during oocyte maturation is crucial for aggregate removal: the sperm-derived signals trigger the acidification of lysosomes, which in turn engulf the aggregates by a process that resembles microautophagy morphologically (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Sperm-derived signals trigger the acidification of lysosomes, which in turn engulf the aggregates by a process that resembles microautophagy morphologically.
source: The shift in lysosomal physiology that occurs during oocyte maturation is crucial for aggregate removal: the sperm-derived signals trigger the acidification of lysosomes, which in turn engulf the aggregates by a process that resembles microautophagy morphologically (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Lysosomal acidification triggers a conversion in mitochondrial dynamics from a poised state characterized by a high membrane potential to an active state in which the membrane potential is reduced.
source: Lysosomal acidification also triggers a conversion in mitochondrial dynamics from what appears to be a poised state, characterized by a high membrane potential, to an active state, in which the membrane potential is reduced.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Inactivation of mitochondrial ATP synthase prevents the mitochondrial membrane potential shift and prevents aggregate removal.
source: Conditions that prevent this mitochondrial membrane potential shift, such as inactivation of mitochondrial ATP synthase, prevent aggregate removal.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: A genome-wide RNAi screen identified 81 genes that influence oocyte protein aggregation.
source: A genome-wide RNAi screen identifies 81 genes that influence oocyte protein aggregation
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Protein aggregates accumulate in young, newly formed oocytes in the absence of sperm.
source: We find that (i) protein aggregates accumulate in young, newly formed oocytes in the absence of sperm—their formation is an integral part of oocyte development rather than a consequence of prolonged oocyte quiescence
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Protein aggregate formation is an integral part of oocyte development rather than a consequence of prolonged oocyte quiescence.
source: We find that (i) protein aggregates accumulate in young, newly formed oocytes in the absence of sperm—their formation is an integral part of oocyte development rather than a consequence of prolonged oocyte quiescence
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Inhibiting processes required for changes in ER morphogenesis and function during oocyte maturation prevents lysosome acidification by preventing the assembly of the V-ATPase lysosomal proton pump.
source: (ii) inhibiting processes required for changes in ER morphogenesis and function during oocyte maturation, including protein synthesis and actin dynamics, prevents lysosome acidification by preventing the assembly of the V-ATPase lysosomal proton pump
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting protein synthesis prevents lysosome acidification by preventing the assembly of the V-ATPase lysosomal proton pump.
source: (ii) inhibiting processes required for changes in ER morphogenesis and function during oocyte maturation, including protein synthesis and actin dynamics, prevents lysosome acidification by preventing the assembly of the V-ATPase lysosomal proton pump
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting actin dynamics prevents lysosome acidification by preventing the assembly of the V-ATPase lysosomal proton pump.
source: (ii) inhibiting processes required for changes in ER morphogenesis and function during oocyte maturation, including protein synthesis and actin dynamics, prevents lysosome acidification by preventing the assembly of the V-ATPase lysosomal proton pump
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Mitochondria elaborate an energy-independent checkpoint that gates protein-aggregate removal.
source: (iii) mitochondria elaborate an energy-independent checkpoint that gates protein-aggregate removal
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) proteins are required for aggregate removal.
source: (iv) endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) proteins are required for aggregate removal, consistent with protein aggregates being removed via microautophagy
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Protein aggregates are removed via microautophagy.
source: (iv) endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) proteins are required for aggregate removal, consistent with protein aggregates being removed via microautophagy
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Inhibiting TRiC-complex chaperonins or HSP70 chaperones promotes protein aggregation indirectly by acting upstream in the pathway to block lysosome acidification.
source: (v) as with proteasome inhibition, inhibiting TRiC-complex chaperonins or HSP70 chaperones promotes protein aggregation indirectly by acting upstream in the pathway to block lysosome acidification.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting proteasome function promotes protein aggregation indirectly by acting upstream in the pathway to block lysosome acidification.
source: (v) as with proteasome inhibition, inhibiting TRiC-complex chaperonins or HSP70 chaperones promotes protein aggregation indirectly by acting upstream in the pathway to block lysosome acidification.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting lysosomal V-ATPase accelerates age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma.
source: Finally, we show that inhibiting lysosomal V-ATPase, vesicle-transport or proteasome function also accelerates age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma, thus bridging mechanisms that enhance proteostasis in the immortal germ lineage to those that maintain proteostasis in the aging soma.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting vesicle-transport accelerates age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma.
source: Finally, we show that inhibiting lysosomal V-ATPase, vesicle-transport or proteasome function also accelerates age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma, thus bridging mechanisms that enhance proteostasis in the immortal germ lineage to those that maintain proteostasis in the aging soma.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting proteasome function accelerates age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma.
source: Finally, we show that inhibiting lysosomal V-ATPase, vesicle-transport or proteasome function also accelerates age-dependent protein aggregation in the soma, thus bridging mechanisms that enhance proteostasis in the immortal germ lineage to those that maintain proteostasis in the aging soma.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The Ahringer RNAi feeding library targets ~87% of annotated C. elegans genes.
source: To undertake an unbiased genome-wide RNAi screen for components of the germline proteostasis network, we utilized the Ahringer RNAi feeding library (Kamath et al., 2003), which targets ~87% of annotated C. elegans genes
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: GFP::RHO-1 forms dense patchy aggregates in female oocytes.
source: A germline-specific GFP::RHO-1 translational fusion was selected as the reporter for the screen as it forms dense patchy aggregates in female oocytes (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: GFP::RHO-1 forms aggregates in unfertilized oocytes of aging hermaphrodites, which deplete their stores of sperm.
source: A germline-specific GFP::RHO-1 translational fusion was selected as the reporter for the screen as it forms dense patchy aggregates in female oocytes (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017) and in unfertilized oocytes of aging hermaphrodites, which deplete their stores of sperm (David et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The primary screen identified 367 genes whose knockdown led to GFP::RHO-1 aggregation in at least 50% of the animals.
source: The primary screen identified 367 genes whose knockdown led to GFP::RHO-1 aggregation in at least 50% of the animals.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The 88 validated genes represented diverse cellular processes.
source: The resulting set of 88 genes represented diverse cellular processes (Supplementary file 1), with highly enriched gene ontology (GO) categories including translation, RNA processing, and cytoskeletal organization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Highly enriched gene ontology (GO) categories included translation, RNA processing, and cytoskeletal organization.
source: The resulting set of 88 genes represented diverse cellular processes (Supplementary file 1), with highly enriched gene ontology (GO) categories including translation, RNA processing, and cytoskeletal organization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: ATP-hydrolysis-coupled proton transport and lysosome acidification were both highly enriched GO categories.
source: In addition, ATP-hydrolysis-coupled proton transport and lysosome acidification were both highly enriched, in agreement with our previous findings (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data, consistent with prior work.

claim: Out of 55 candidates tested, 53 RNAi knockdowns also caused NMY-2::GFP protein-aggregate accumulation.
source: Out of the 55 candidates tested, 53 RNAi knockdowns also caused NMY-2::GFP protein-aggregate accumulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The validated genes are likely to have a general effect on protein-aggregate clearance rather than a specific effect on GFP::RHO-1.
source: Thus, these genes are likely to have a general effect on protein-aggregate clearance rather than a specific effect on GFP::RHO-1.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Age-matched first-proximal oocytes of young females often contained protein aggregates.
source: We found that age-matched first-proximal oocytes of young females often contained protein aggregates (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Protein-aggregate accumulation does not require prolonged oocyte quiescence; instead, it appears to be part of the normal developmental sequence of oocytes that are not exposed to sperm.
source: Therefore, protein-aggregate accumulation does not require prolonged oocyte quiescence; instead, it appears to be part of the normal developmental sequence of oocytes that are not exposed to sperm.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The ER undergoes a major morphological rearrangement in response to oocyte maturation signals.
source: The ER undergoes a major morphological rearrangement in response to oocyte maturation signals (Langerak et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In hermaphrodite oocytes, the ER assumed a fine network appearance, whereas in female oocytes, the ER formed bright, distinctive patches.
source: In hermaphrodite oocytes, the ER assumed a fine network appearance, whereas in female oocytes, the ER formed bright, distinctive patches (Figure 2A, C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Pristine female oocytes exhibited ER patches, indicating that the altered ER architecture is an intrinsic property of female oocytes and not a consequence of prolonged quiescence.
source: Pristine female oocytes also exhibited ER patches, indicating that the altered ER architecture is an intrinsic property of female oocytes and not a consequence of prolonged quiescence (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: In female oocytes the ER and GFP::RHO-1 aggregates segregated spatially into mutually exclusive regions.
source: Using two fluorescent reporters, we visualized both the ER and GFP::RHO-1 simultaneously (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) and found that in female oocytes the ER and GFP::RHO-1 aggregates segregated spatially into mutually exclusive regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The ER in pristine oocytes from both sexes appeared to be associated with ribosomes, indicative of active (or poised) protein synthesis.
source: The ER in pristine oocytes from both sexes appeared to be associated with ribosomes, indicative of active (or poised) protein synthesis, yet the female ER was distinctively clustered into parallel stacks (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data (TEM) and shown in figures.

claim: The female ER was distinctively clustered into parallel stacks.
source: The ER in pristine oocytes from both sexes appeared to be associated with ribosomes, indicative of active (or poised) protein synthesis, yet the female ER was distinctively clustered into parallel stacks (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data (TEM) and shown in figures.

claim: The presence of sperm triggered distinctive remodeling of the ER architecture and the clearance of aggregates, although with different kinetics.
source: The presence of sperm triggered distinctive remodeling of the ER architecture and the clearance of aggregates, although with different kinetics (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The earliest changes in the ER were detected approximately 10 min after mating, and the morphology was significantly altered by 30 min.
source: The earliest changes in the ER were detected approximately 10 min after mating, and the morphology was significantly altered by 30 min (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The clearance of NMY-2 aggregates started a few minutes later, with aggregate clearance in the most proximal oocytes typically occurring between 20 and 30 min after mating.
source: In contrast, the clearance of NMY-2 aggregates started a few minutes later, with aggregate clearance in the most proximal oocytes typically occurring between 20 and 30 min after mating (Figure 2—figure supplement 4, 5, 6A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Genes involved in cytoskeletal organization, protein synthesis and protein folding were required for maintaining normal ER morphology and led to an altered ER architecture when knocked down.
source: Genes involved in cytoskeletal organization, protein synthesis and protein folding were required for maintaining normal ER morphology and led to an altered ER architecture when knocked down.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Disrupting the mitochondrial ATP synthase, the V-ATPase complex, or ER function itself did not visibly alter the ER network.
source: Notably, disrupting the mitochondrial ATP synthase, the V-ATPase complex, or ER function itself did not visibly alter the ER network, suggesting that these gene functions were not required for the sperm-induced ER morphology change, or more generally for ER morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Signals from sperm elicit the lysosomal acidification required for the clearance of protein aggregates.
source: Signals from sperm elicit the lysosomal acidification required for the clearance of protein aggregates, and inhibiting the V-ATPase, which acidifies lysosomes, causes proteins to aggregate in hermaphrodite oocytes (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Inhibiting the V-ATPase, which acidifies lysosomes, causes proteins to aggregate in hermaphrodite oocytes.
source: Signals from sperm elicit the lysosomal acidification required for the clearance of protein aggregates, and inhibiting the V-ATPase, which acidifies lysosomes, causes proteins to aggregate in hermaphrodite oocytes (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: None of the endogenously tagged V-ATPase subunits were visible in the germline in either intact animals or in their dissected gonads.
source: Unexpectedly, although each one of these tagged proteins was visible in somatic tissues, we were unable to detect any fluorescence in the germline in either intact animals (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) or in their dissected gonads (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: V-ATPase subunits are expressed and required in the germline.
source: Both wild-type and germline-RNAi-permissive DCL569 animals exhibited sterility when fed vha-12 and vha-13 RNAi bacteria (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), whereas the whole-body RNAi-defective rde-1 mutant did not. Thus, these V-ATPase subunits are expressed and required in the germline, despite our inability to detect them when tagged endogenously.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: GFP::VHA-13 formed distinct foci in hermaphrodite oocytes that colocalized with foci of LysoTracker.
source: In these animals, we observed a striking, sperm-dependent pattern: GFP::VHA-13 formed distinct foci in hermaphrodite oocytes (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) that colocalized with foci of LysoTracker, a dye that stains acidic lysosomes (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The proximal oocytes of females exhibited a diffuse GFP::VHA-13 fluorescent signal.
source: In contrast, the proximal oocytes of females exhibited a diffuse GFP::VHA-13 fluorescent signal (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 3B), with a slight enrichment in the perinuclear region.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Female oocytes demonstrated very weak LysoTracker staining, and there was no significant overlap in the two signals.
source: Female oocytes demonstrated very weak LysoTracker staining (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017), and there was no significant overlap in the two signals (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures, with a citation to prior work.

claim: Even at the limit of fluorescence detection, hermaphrodites still exhibited GFP::VHA-13 foci, and females exhibited a diffuse distribution.
source: Even at the limit of fluorescence detection, hermaphrodites still exhibited GFP::VHA-13 foci, and females exhibited a diffuse distribution (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The germline harbors a mechanism by which VHA-13 is localized to discrete, acidic cellular locations, indicative of lysosomes, only in the presence of sperm.
source: Thus, the germline harbors a mechanism by which VHA-13 is localized to discrete, acidic cellular locations, indicative of lysosomes, only in the presence of sperm.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Knocking down the vha-12 gene prevented GFP::VHA-13 foci formation in hermaphrodite oocytes.
source: Notably, knocking down the vha-12 gene, which encodes another peripheral V-ATPase V1-domain subunit, also prevented GFP::VHA-13 foci formation in hermaphrodite oocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D), suggesting a coordinated assembly pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Knocking down vha-12 suggests a coordinated assembly pathway for V-ATPase subunits.
source: Notably, knocking down the vha-12 gene, which encodes another peripheral V-ATPase V1-domain subunit, also prevented GFP::VHA-13 foci formation in hermaphrodite oocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D), suggesting a coordinated assembly pathway.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Older, sperm-depleted hermaphrodites (day 5) exhibited diffuse V-ATPase localization, similar to that of females.
source: First, we examined older, sperm-depleted hermaphrodites (day 5) and observed diffuse V-ATPase localization, similar to that of females (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The diffuse fluorescent signal of GFP::VHA-13 in female oocytes began to change approximately 10 min after mating, organizing into distinct foci within 20–30 min.
source: The diffuse fluorescent signal began to change approximately 10 min after mating, organizing into distinct foci within 20–30 min (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The time scales of ER remodeling and GFP::VHA-13 relocalization were strikingly similar, suggesting a possible causal relationship.
source: The time scales of ER remodeling and GFP::VHA-13 relocalization (Figure 2E) were strikingly similar, suggesting a possible causal relationship.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Sperm signals lead to lysosome acidification by initiating the recruitment of V-ATPase subunits to the surface of the lysosome and enabling proton-pump assembly.
source: Together, these findings suggest that sperm signals lead to lysosome acidification by initiating the recruitment of V-ATPase subunits to the surface of the lysosome and enabling proton-pump assembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The great majority of gene inhibitions prevented lysosome acidification.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that the great majority of gene inhibitions prevented lysosome acidification (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The ATP synthase genes atp-2 and atp-3 were the only exceptions that did not prevent lysosome acidification.
source: The ATP synthase genes atp-2 and atp-3 were the only exceptions, consistent with previous observations suggesting that mitochondrial ATP-synthase activity acts downstream of lysosome acidification to prevent protein aggregation (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data, consistent with prior work.

claim: Mitochondrial ATP-synthase activity acts downstream of lysosome acidification to prevent protein aggregation.
source: The ATP synthase genes atp-2 and atp-3 were the only exceptions, consistent with previous observations suggesting that mitochondrial ATP-synthase activity acts downstream of lysosome acidification to prevent protein aggregation (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: All of the knockdowns that blocked lysosome acidification showed reduced GFP::VHA-13 skewness.
source: All of the knockdowns that blocked lysosome acidification showed reduced GFP::VHA-13 skewness, albeit to varying degrees.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Neither of the two ATP synthase gene knockdowns affected GFP::VHA-13 puncta formation.
source: As anticipated, neither of the two ATP synthase gene knockdowns affected GFP::VHA-13 puncta formation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The failure of the gene knockdowns to acidify lysosomes is due, at least in part, to a failure to assemble the lysosomal V-ATPase.
source: Together, these data support the model that the failure of the gene knockdowns to acidify lysosomes is due, at least in part, to a failure to assemble the lysosomal V-ATPase.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Mitochondria undergo a morphological and metabolic shift in response to signals from sperm, a shift that is required for aggregate removal.
source: Mitochondria undergo a morphological and metabolic shift in response to signals from sperm, a shift that is required for aggregate removal (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Unfertilized female oocytes exhibit a high mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨ) relative to hermaphrodite oocytes or to female oocytes exposed to sperm by mating.
source: Unfertilized female oocytes exhibit a high mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨ) relative to hermaphrodite oocytes or to female oocytes exposed to sperm by mating.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Loss of the mitochondrial ATP synthase elevates ΔΨ in hermaphrodites and causes protein aggregates to accumulate.
source: Loss of the mitochondrial ATP synthase, which discharges the proton gradient during the generation of ATP, elevates ΔΨ in hermaphrodites and causes protein aggregates to accumulate (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Lysosomal V-ATPase activity was required for the shift in mitochondrial membrane potential.
source: Previously, we found that lysosomal V-ATPase activity was required for the shift in mitochondrial membrane potential (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: All of the knockdowns prevented the ΔΨ decrease in proximal hermaphrodite oocytes.
source: As predicted, all of the knockdowns prevented the ΔΨ decrease in proximal hermaphrodite oocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: In many cases the mitochondria exhibited ΔΨ ratios even higher than those of females.
source: Unexpectedly, in many cases the mitochondria exhibited ΔΨ ratios even higher than those of females (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that the female oocyte ΔΨ is not the default state, but potentially an optimal point within a broader range of possibilities.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The female oocyte ΔΨ is not the default state, but potentially an optimal point within a broader range of possibilities.
source: Unexpectedly, in many cases the mitochondria exhibited ΔΨ ratios even higher than those of females (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that the female oocyte ΔΨ is not the default state, but potentially an optimal point within a broader range of possibilities.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Neither cyc-1 nor nuo-2 RNAi prevented females from accumulating aggregates, even though ΔΨ was reduced.
source: However, neither cyc-1 nor nuo-2 RNAi prevented females from accumulating aggregates, even though ΔΨ was reduced (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: A high mitochondrial membrane potential is not a prerequisite for protein aggregation.
source: Thus, a high mitochondrial membrane potential is not a prerequisite for protein aggregation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: RNAi inhibition of ATP synthase has been shown to reduce ATP levels in worms, as does RNAi inhibition of electron transport.
source: RNAi inhibition of ATP synthase has been shown to reduce ATP levels in worms, as does RNAi inhibition of electron transport (Dillin et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: ETC knockdowns reduced oocyte ATP levels, body size, growth rate, and brood size, but did not cause protein aggregation in hermaphrodite oocytes.
source: The treatments reduced oocyte ATP levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and reduced body size and growth rate (Figure 5B), two known correlates of reduced ATP levels. However, these perturbations did not cause protein aggregation in hermaphrodite oocytes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Loss of ATP synthase causes aggregates to accumulate in hermaphrodites not because it limits ATP levels, but for a different reason.
source: This finding suggests the interesting hypothesis that loss of ATP synthase causes aggregates to accumulate in hermaphrodites not because it limits ATP levels, but for a different reason (see Discussion).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase (ogdh-1) and succinate dehydrogenase (sdhd-1) RNAi led to oocyte GFP::RHO-1 aggregation.
source: We tested several additional Krebs cycle gene knockdowns (pdha-1, idhg-1, ogdh-1, sucl-1, and sdhd-1) and found that α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase (ogdh-1) and succinate dehydrogenase (sdhd-1) RNAi also led to oocyte GFP::RHO-1 aggregation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Unlike ATP synthase inhibition, aco-2 inhibition prevented lysosome acidification.
source: Notably, unlike ATP synthase inhibition, aco-2 inhibition prevented lysosome acidification (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the Krebs cycle and ATP synthase likely have distinct roles in the protein-aggregation pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The Krebs cycle and ATP synthase likely have distinct roles in the protein-aggregation pathway.
source: Notably, unlike ATP synthase inhibition, aco-2 inhibition prevented lysosome acidification (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the Krebs cycle and ATP synthase likely have distinct roles in the protein-aggregation pathway.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Lysosomes engulf protein aggregates in a process reminiscent of microautophagy.
source: Previously, we observed lysosomes engulfing protein aggregates in a process reminiscent of microautophagy (Bohnert and Kenyon, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Microautophagy had not been described previously in C. elegans.
source: Before these observations, microautophagy had not been described in C. elegans.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current study.

claim: Inhibiting ESCRT-complex members prevents aggregate accumulation in maturing C. elegans oocytes.
source: In this study, using a candidate approach, we showed that inhibiting ESCRT-complex members, which are known to mediate microautophagy in other organisms, prevents aggregate accumulation in maturing C. elegans oocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: ESCRT-complex members influence protein aggregation independently of lysosomal acidification.
source: Moreover, they influence protein aggregation independently of lysosomal acidification, consistent with their having a direct role.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: Microautophagy is an active proteostasis mechanism in C. elegans, and likely the mechanism by which aggregates are cleared in response to oocyte maturation signals.
source: These findings strengthen the case that microautophagy is an active proteostasis mechanism in C. elegans, and likely the mechanism by which aggregates are cleared in response to oocyte maturation signals (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The screen hits that affected the lysosomal V-ATPase and COPII had a striking ability to accelerate age-dependent protein aggregation in somatic cells.
source: Notably, the screen hits that affected the lysosomal V-ATPase and COPII (ER-to-lysosomal vesicle transport) had a striking ability to accelerate age-dependent protein aggregation in somatic cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data.

claim: The same mechanisms that enhance oocyte proteostasis in the immortal germline likely enhance somatic proteostasis as well.
source: Thus, the same mechanisms that enhance oocyte proteostasis in the immortal germline likely enhance somatic proteostasis as well.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: In yeast, lysosomal acidity declines with age, and overexpressing the yeast ortholog of the C. elegans V-ATPase gene vha-13 delays this decline and extends replicative lifespan.
source: In yeast, lysosomal acidity declines with age, and overexpressing the yeast ortholog of the C. elegans V-ATPase gene vha-13 delays this decline and extends replicative lifespan (Hughes and Gottschling, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In worms, lysosome acidification declines with age, and this decline is delayed in long-lived mutants.
source: In worms, lysosome acidification also declines with age, and this decline is delayed in long-lived mutants (Baxi et al., 2017; Sun et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Overproduction of the transcription factor HLH-30/TFEB, which augments many lysosomal functions, extends lifespan in C. elegans.
source: Whether increasing V-ATPase function might be sufficient to extend lifespan in C. elegans is unclear, but overproduction of the transcription factor HLH-30/TFEB, which augments many lysosomal functions, has been shown to do so (Lapierre et al., 2013; O'Rourke and Ruvkun, 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In mammals, similar perturbations slow the aging of the immune system.
source: and in mammals, similar perturbations slow the aging of the immune system (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The ESCRT subunits vps-20, vps-28, vps-37, and vps-54 tested positive with subtle aggregation phenotypes.
source: In these experiments, the ESCRT subunits vps-20, vps-28, vps-37, and vps-54 tested positive with subtle aggregation phenotypes (although not observed in all animals tested) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The degree of GFP::VHA-13 localization to puncta in ESCRT knockdowns was comparable to that of hermaphrodites.
source: Importantly, the degree of GFP::VHA-13 localization to puncta in these knockdowns was comparable to that of hermaphrodites (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B, C)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: ESCRT knockdowns permitted acidification of oocyte lysosomes.
source: and they also permitted acidification of oocyte lysosomes (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The ESCRT machinery operates downstream of V-ATPase assembly and lysosome acidification to prevent aggregate accumulation.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that the ESCRT machinery operates downstream of V-ATPase assembly and lysosome acidification to prevent aggregate accumulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Multiple RNAi knockdowns that impaired lysosomal acidification in the germline-induced premature KIN-19::split-wrmScarlet aggregation in the soma.
source: We found that multiple RNAi knockdowns that impaired lysosomal acidification in the germline-induced premature KIN-19::split-wrmScarlet aggregation in the soma, most notably RNAi of genes encoding lysosomal V-ATPase subunits (vha-12, vha-13, vha-16, and vha-19), but also genes that, in the germline, were required for V-ATPase assembly (the actin gene act-5 and the vesicle-mediated ER-to-Golgi transport gene copb-2) (Figure 6C, D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The knockdowns affected lysosome acidification in the intestine, where the RNAi treatment led to fewer discrete acidic lysosome-related organelles, thereby reducing the skewness of the LysoTracker signal.
source: We were not able to visualize lysosome acidification in the head using LysoTracker, but these knockdowns did affect lysosome acidification in the intestine, where the RNAi treatment led to fewer discrete acidic lysosome-related organelles, thereby reducing the skewness of the LysoTracker signal (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: The proteasome subunits pbs-7 and rpn-6.1 were recovered, indicating a direct or indirect role for proteasome function to maintain KIN-19 solubility in the aging soma.
source: We also recovered the proteasome subunits pbs-7 and rpn-6.1, indicating a direct or indirect role for proteasome function to maintain KIN-19 solubility in the aging soma (Figure 6C, D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: vha-12 and vha-19 knockdowns accelerated the timing of age-related Q35::YFP aggregation.
source: Similar to KIN-19::split-wrmScarlet, vha-12 and vha-19 knockdowns accelerated the timing of age-related Q35::YFP aggregation, as did copb-2 and rpn-6.1 RNAi (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Knocking down one of the four ESCRT-complex subunits tested, vps-37, led to Q35::YFP aggregation.
source: Further, knocking down one of the four ESCRT-complex subunits we tested, vps-37, also led to Q35::YFP aggregation (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: None of the ESCRT gene knockdowns accelerated the KIN-19::split-wrmScarlet somatic aggregation, even in animals exposed to RNAi from the first larval stage.
source: In contrast, none of the ESCRT gene knockdowns accelerated the KIN-19::split-wrmScarlet somatic aggregation, even in animals exposed to RNAi from the first larval stage, despite a significant decrease in mRNA levels in the two subunits measured (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the current study based on experimental data and shown in figures.

claim: Lysosomal microautophagy may prevent the accumulation of Q35::YFP aggregates.
source: Together, these findings suggest that lysosomal microautophagy may prevent the accumulation of Q35::YFP aggregates, but future studies will be required for certainty.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.
